headline: Bill Gates said on CNN that, in the years ahead, society will have to decide how to tax AI and robot use and which jobs to keep for humans.
score_reason: Pool 7 lowered to 6: 'calls for taxing AI' overstates it, since Gates said society must decide 'in the years ahead' and gave no proposal, rate or date.
importance_line: What changed is that a leading voice on AI put taxing AI and human-only jobs back on the public agenda, which would affect workers in fields such as education and health care first, then governments that would design any tax, then AI companies, but it is an opinion in an interview with no proposal, rate or timetable behind it.
summary: ETHRWorld reports, relaying the Microsoft co-founder's interview on CNN's State of the Union on 11 Oct 2026, that Bill Gates said society must decide how to tax AI or robot use and where to preserve human jobs, and that reserving work for people "may sound bizarre" now but "we will get there". He also named cyberattacks by bad actors as the most immediate danger and said he expects AI companies to stop being their own only check within a year, with government safety bodies like those for aviation and medicines.
notes: ETHRWorld's own page gave only its opening paragraph; the detail is from Telangana Today and FourWeekMBA accounts of the same CNN interview (FourWeekMBA says it read CNN's rush transcript). CNN's page was not opened, so the url stays on ETHRWorld. Gates's Reuters interview was in our 9 Oct 2026 edition; this is a different interview with new remarks.
